title: Elon and the Physics of Wonder
subtitle: Ask why, then try
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia visits a sunny workshop, where Elon turns falling apples, magnets and paper rockets into physics she can touch.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

grok.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: The workshop
pages.text: {Olivia} pushed open the {workshop} door. {Elon:elon/wave} looked up from a chalkboard. "Hello," he said. "Today we {ask:olivia/ask} why. Then we {try:elon/teach}."
pages.hint: Tap Elon. Tap Olivia. Tap the little rocket.

pages.heading: Why things fall
pages.text: An {apple:apple/fall} hung in the air. "Let go," said {Elon:elon/look}. The apple {fell:apple/drop}. "That pull is {gravity}," said Elon. "The Earth is hugging everything."
pages.hint: Tap the apple and watch it fall.

pages.heading: Push, and it pushes back
pages.text: "A {rocket:rocket/push} does not fly by magic," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "It {pushes:rocket/fly} the air down. The air {pushes} the rocket up. Every action has a partner."
pages.hint: Tap the rocket. Watch it lift.

pages.heading: Invisible hands
pages.text: {Olivia:olivia/ask} held a {magnet:magnet/pull}. It tugged without touching. "Some forces you cannot see," said {Elon:elon/look}. "Electricity is a river of tiny sparks. Magnets are their quiet cousins."

pages.heading: Suns far away
pages.text: They stood under a chalkboard {sky:stars/glow}. "{Stars:stars/glow} are suns," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "They look small because they are very far. Light is the fastest thing we know."

pages.heading: Try
pages.text: "Now we {try:rocket/fly}," said {Elon:elon/wave}. {Olivia:olivia/run} counted. Three, two, one. The paper {rocket:rocket/fly} hopped, then {flew}. Physics is a promise you can test.

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: The sun went gold in the {workshop} window. "The best engine is a question," said {Elon:elon/teach}. {Olivia:olivia/ask} smiled. "Why?" "Yes," said Elon. "That one. Keep it."

end.heading: The End
end.text: You {read} a whole {story} of falling, pushing and stars. Ask why. Then try.
end.prompt: If you could test one question tomorrow, what would it be?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf from a family photo of Olivia. A picture-book inventor teaches physics; this is not a biography.

questions.right: Yes! Gravity is the Earth's hug. It pulls the apple down.
questions.wrong: Not quite. Elon called that pull gravity.

questions.q: How does a rocket go up?

options.label: it pushes, and the air pushes back
